chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is not befitting for the man to leave behind (for someone) the butter for oil, nor the oil for the butter'.

key_terms.إِسْلَافُ: To leave behind or give in place of (a specific item or debt)
key_terms.لَا يَنْبَغِي: It is not befitting / not permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging butter for oil in Islamic trade?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi addresses the prohibition of *islaf* (deferred exchange) between butter and oil, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on preventing *gharar* (uncertainty) and *riba* (usury) in commodity trades where quality and measure may differ. It underscores the principle of fairness in commercial transactions by ensuring that deferred payments do not exploit discrepancies in the specific attributes of the goods exchanged.
